stories.headline: Iran and Oman discuss temporary shipping lane in Strait of Hormuz
stories.body:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi in Tehran for talks about shipping. The two officials discussed an interim framework for ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

A joint statement carried by the Oman News Agency said Iran and Oman want to establish a temporary joint maritime corridor. The two nations also plan a mine clearance project in the strait.

War broke out on February 28 after the US and Israel attacked Iran. Iran blockaded the Strait of Hormuz. Washington then placed a naval counter-blockade on Iranian ports. A 60-day peace deal between Iran and the US ended in mid-August.

US President Donald Trump said on social media that the US Navy cleared mines from the strait. Trump warned that any boat placing new mines will be destroyed immediately. On August 25, an unidentified projectile struck an oil tanker at the mouth of the strait. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre reported the attack.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced sanctions on 60 people, entities, and vessels trading with Iran. Chinese buyers take about 90% of Iranian oil exports, according to reporting by the Financial Times. China's foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said China will firmly safeguard its rights.

claims.text: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi held talks in Tehran regarding an interim framework for shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
A joint statement carried by the Oman News Agency stated that Iran and Oman seek to establish a temporary joint maritime corridor and a mine clearance project in the Strait of Hormuz.
War broke out on February 28 after the US and Israel attacked Iran, prompting Tehran to blockade the Strait of Hormuz and Washington to impose a naval counter-blockade on Iranian ports.
A 60-day interim peace deal signed by Iran and the US in June ended in mid-August.
US President Donald Trump stated on social media that the US Navy cleared mines from the Strait of Hormuz.
US President Donald Trump stated: "Iran has been notified that any ship or boat placing new mines will be immediately and systematically destroyed."
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre reported that an oil tanker was struck by an unidentified projectile at the mouth of the Strait of Hormuz on August 25.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced an initial set of US sanctions targeting 60 individuals, entities, and vessels for alleged involvement in trade with Iran.
Chinese buyers account for about 90% of Iran's oil exports, according to reporting by the Financial Times.
China's foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian stated: "China will take all necessary measures to firmly safeguard its own rights and interests."

stories.headline: Canada places retaliatory tariffs up to 50% on US goods
stories.body:
Canada announced retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% on US goods starting September 8. The new measures target $20 billion worth of American imports.

The trade dispute between the two nations has grown deeper. The new Canadian tariffs will impose duties across many goods. One report said the duties cover 700 products. Another report said the counter-tariffs apply to nearly 900 items. These items equal nearly C$28 billion in value. That amount equals $20 billion.

The tariffs include a 50% duty on American steel and aluminum. Canadian officials said that US steel imports to Canada have already fallen 30%. That fall happened after Canada introduced an earlier 25% tariff.

The political leaders of both countries have exchanged strong statements. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney accused US President Donald Trump of wanting to destroy Canadian industries. President Trump suggested on social media that he may change the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America. Trump made the comment on Truth Social.

Trump also said his administration will raise tariffs on Canadian goods in the future. He said US tariffs on Canadian vehicles, automotive parts, and steel will rise to 50%. That increase is set to start on January 1, 2027.

Trade between the two neighbours remains large. Canada maintains a trade surplus with the US of C$9.9 billion. According to Statistics Canada, that trade surplus equals $7.1 billion.

To protect the domestic economy, the Canadian government announced financial aid. Canadian Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne announced an additional C$7.5 billion support package. The funds will support businesses and workers impacted by US tariffs.

Canadian Industry Minister Mélanie Joly outlined details of the C$7.5 billion support package. The aid plan includes C$3 million in grants. It also includes C$2 million in interest-free loans for small businesses.

The new Canadian tariffs will impose duties across 700 products, including a 50% duty on American steel and aluminum.
Canada's counter-tariffs will apply to nearly C$28 billion ($20 billion) worth of US products across nearly 900 items.
Canadian officials stated US steel imports to Canada have fallen 30% since Canada introduced a 25% tariff.

US President Donald Trump suggested on Truth Social that he may change the name of Lake Ontario to "Lake America".

stories.headline: CIA Director John Ratcliffe makes unannounced trip to Moscow
stories.body:
CIA Director John Ratcliffe made an unannounced visit to Moscow on August 25 for talks with Russian officials. CBS News first reported the trip.

Tracking data from FlightRadar24 showed a US military C-17 plane left Riga at 05:50 GMT. The aircraft landed in Moscow at 07:04 GMT. It flew back to Riga shortly before 17:00 GMT on August 25. The US Air Force Boeing C-17A Globemaster III started its journey from Joint Base Andrews in Maryland. It landed at Moscow's Vnukovo International Airport.

A senior Ukrainian official told CBS News that the US notified Kyiv about the visit. The US requested Ukraine to pause strikes until the delegation left. The Financial Times reported the Trump administration asked Kyiv to pause long-range strikes on major Russian cities during the visit. But Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said no talks with US envoys were planned for the week.

This trip is the first known visit by a US spy chief to Moscow since former CIA Director William Burns visited in November 2021.

FlightRadar24 tracking data showed a US military C-17 aircraft departed Riga at 05:50 GMT, landed in Moscow at 07:04 GMT, and returned to Riga shortly before 17:00 GMT on August 25.
A US Air Force Boeing C-17A Globemaster III military transport aircraft flew from Riga, Latvia, to Moscow's Vnukovo International Airport after originating from Joint Base Andrews in Maryland.
A senior Ukrainian official told CBS News that the US notified Kyiv of a senior delegation visiting Moscow and requested Ukraine to suspend strikes until the delegation left.
The Financial Times reported that the Trump administration requested Kyiv to pause long-range strikes on major Russian cities during CIA Director John Ratcliffe's visit to Moscow.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov stated on August 25 that no talks between Moscow and US envoys were planned for the week.
CIA Director John Ratcliffe's trip marks the first known visit by a US spy chief to Moscow since former CIA Director William Burns visited in November 2021.

stories.headline: US sanctions four Indian companies over Iranian petroleum imports
stories.body:
The United States Department of State sanctioned four Indian companies for importing Iranian petroleum products. The sanctions were issued under Operation Economic Outcast. They used Executive Orders 13846 and 13949.

The US targeted Portease Partners, Sadashiva Overseas, PP Softtech, and Prakrutees Infra Impex. Three individuals were also sanctioned. They are Portease partners Indrismiya Ashrafmiya Sheikh and Harish Ramachandra Rangi, and PP Softtech director Prashant Garg.

The US Department of State said Sadashiva Overseas imported about $69 million worth of Iranian petroleum products. That trade took place between February 2024 and June 2025. PP Softtech and Prakrutees Infra each imported about $25 million worth. PP Softtech imported products between January 2024 and June 2025. Prakrutees Infra imported products between May 2023 and February 2026.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the goal is to sever every economic lifeline sustaining Iran. Iranian Economy Minister Ali Madanizadeh told state television that Tehran was fully prepared for the new sanctions.

claims.text: The United States sanctioned four India-based companies—Portease Partners LLP, Sadashiva Overseas Limited, PP Softtech Private Limited, and Prakrutees Infra Impex Private Limited—for importing petroleum and petrochemical products from Iran.
The United States Department of State announced 'Operation Economic Outcast', targeting Iran's military activities, procurement networks, and petroleum and petrochemical traders with fresh sanctions.
The US sanctions under Operation Economic Outcast were issued under Executive Orders 13846 and 13949.

Indian citizens Indrismiya Ashrafmiya Sheikh and Harish Ramachandra Rangi, partners of Portease Partners LLP, and Prashant Garg, director of PP Softtech Private Limited, were individually sanctioned by the United States.
The US Department of State alleged that Sadashiva Overseas imported about $69 million worth of Iranian-origin petroleum products.
Sadashiva Overseas Limited imported approximately $69 million worth of Iranian-origin petroleum products between February 2024 and June 2025.
The US Department of State alleged that PP Softtech and Prakrutees Infra each imported about $25 million worth of Iranian petroleum products.
PP Softtech Private Limited imported approximately $25 million worth of Iranian petroleum products between January 2024 and June 2025.
Prakrutees Infra Impex India Private Limited imported Iranian petroleum products worth approximately $25 million between May 2023 and February 2026.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that the objective of the sanctions was 'to sever every economic lifeline' sustaining Iran.
Iranian Economy Minister Ali Madanizadeh told state television that Tehran was 'fully prepared' for the newly imposed sanctions.

stories.headline: Ajit Doval and Wang Yi hold border talks in Beijing
stories.body:
Indian National Security Advisor Ajit Doval met Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Beijing for border talks. The meeting marked the 25th round of Special Representatives talks on the India-China boundary question.

Both countries discussed their long-standing border issue. India and China agreed to continue seeking a political settlement of the boundary question. They agreed to do this in the context of their overall and long-term interests.

During the talks, Doval spoke about progress on local trade and travel. Doval said that the Kailash Manasarovar Yatra via Nathu La has successfully resumed. He also said that traditional border trade via all three passes has successfully resumed.

Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi spoke about the broader importance of ties between the two nations. Wang said that the China-India relationship has gone beyond the bilateral scope. He said the relationship has taken on global and strategic significance. Wang also called for gradually building a positive narrative on boundary affairs between India and China.

Before holding the main border talks, Doval met another senior Chinese leader. Doval held a bilateral meeting with Chinese Vice President Han Zheng in Beijing on August 25. That meeting took place before the Special Representatives border talks.

Chinese Ambassador to India Xu Feihong shared details about that meeting. Xu said that Vice President Han highlighted earlier high-level contacts between the two nations. Han highlighted meetings between Chinese President Xi Jinping and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Those meetings took place in Kazan and Tianjin over the past two years.

stories.headline: Student protesters clash with police in Bihar over job exams
stories.body:
Student protesters clashed with police in Patna on August 25 during a march toward the Chief Minister's residence. The march was heading toward Lok Sevak Awas, the official home of the Chief Minister.

Police used batons and water cannons after protesters broke through barricades at Dak Bungalow Chowk. A Deputy Superintendent of Police was severely injured after being hit by thrown stones. Police detained at least 25 protesters in Patna before releasing them later.

The protests follow a government job announcement. The Bihar government issued a notification on August 18 for 32,388 teaching posts. The posts are to be filled through the Teacher Recruitment Examination. Protesting students demanded the exam be held in a single phase without negative marks.

Bihar Public Service Commission Examination Controller Rajesh Kumar Singh expressed regret over comments he made. He had quoted a Hindi proverb that students interpreted as calling them dogs.

Student representatives met Bihar top bureaucrat Pratyaya Amrit. Amrit assured them of a favourable response within a couple of days.

Police used batons and water cannons after student protesters broke through barricades at Dak Bungalow Chowk in Patna.
A Deputy Superintendent of Police was severely injured after being hit by stones thrown during the Patna protest.
Police in Bihar detained at least 25 protesters in Patna during the demonstrations before later releasing them.
The Bihar government issued a notification on August 18 for 32,388 teaching posts to be filled through the Teacher Recruitment Examination.
Protesting students demanded that the Teacher Recruitment Examination be conducted in a single phase without negative marks rather than in two rounds.
Bihar Public Service Commission Examination Controller Rajesh Kumar Singh expressed regret after quoting a Hindi proverb that students interpreted as calling them 'dogs'.
A delegation of student representatives met Bihar top bureaucrat Pratyaya Amrit, who assured them of a favourable response within a couple of days.
